Adobe today announced the launch of a beta version of AI Assisted Editor, a brand new optional editing mode in Photoshop that uses a simplified, prompt-based interface for image editing. Here's what's new.

Photoshop gets optional AI Assisted Editor

Adobe has announced AI Assisted Editor, a brand new beta experience that will swap Photoshop's traditionally detailed and complex image editing tools for a prompt-based interface and simplified menus.

Users can find AI Assisted Editor via a new toggle in the Photoshop menu bar, and can also choose to hide it in settings at any time.

Once in AI Assisted Mode, users will see a simplified interface that includes the following tools:

AI Assisted Editor includes:

Prompt to Edit: Transform images using natural language prompts, no complex manual editing required. Remove Background: Remove backgrounds, clean up edges, and customize images with a few clicks. Generative Expand: Extend image dimensions and generate content that naturally blends into the composition. Remove Tool: Eliminate unwanted objects and distracting elements while preserving image realism. Generative Fill: Add, replace, or remove content with simple text prompts. Generative Upscale: Boost image resolution while maintaining sharpness and visual quality. AI Markup: Mark up images to visually communicate editing instructions for more precise results.

For users new to image editing, or experienced users who need to work with rough concepts and want to quickly sketch out changes, the Markup tool is particularly useful. Users can simply draw or click on any area of the image, then add a natural language instruction such as "add more clouds," "change these shoes," or "add a banner that says ON SALE NOW."

Adobe Firefly will then make the adjustments, and users can continue to fine-tune the results in AI Assisted Edit mode, or switch to the traditional Pro Editor for further refinement.

Other details announced today

In addition to the new optional AI Assisted Editor beta, Photoshop is also gaining prompt-based masking editing, allowing users to roughly select the portion of an image they want Firefly Image 5 to edit.

Adobe says this feature responds to criticism of many existing prompt-based editors, as current versions sometimes degrade image quality, or produce results that don't quite match the overall lighting or subject angle.

Another new feature landing in Photoshop today is a non-destructive layer tool for adjusting light, including adjustments for exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, and blacks. Adobe says: "This lets you achieve Camera Raw-quality results without leaving the Photoshop layers workflow."

A new tool that's the polar opposite of masking-style editing tools is "Prompt to Edit," which lets users write a single prompt to change an entire image, rather than just one portion.

For example, users might want to turn a daytime photo into a nighttime one, or a rainy photo into a sunny one — this tool can help you do that.

This new tool supports FLUX 2 pro, FLUX Context Pro, Gemini 3.1 (with Nano Banana 2), Gemini 3 (with Nano Banana Pro), Gemini 2.5 (with Nano Banana), GPT Image 2, and Adobe's own models, and will create a new layer containing two edited variations of the image.

Finally, Adobe also announced two new features designed to give users "more control, less distraction":

Dynamic Text, Shapes and Paths extends Photoshop's Dynamic Text to any custom shape or path, allowing text to automatically adapt along curves and freeform layouts, so you can preserve original formatting without manual tweaking. Stock Panel Integration brings over 900 million Adobe Stock assets directly into Photoshop as a dockable panel, letting you easily find, preview, and use assets within your workflow.

AI Assisted Editor launches today as a beta, while the other tools are generally available starting today.
